items: Secure Your Company Email: Export and screenshot all relevant company emails immediately, including sent messages, received communications, and folder organization with visible dates and times before your access is revoked.

Capture Messaging Platform Conversations: Screenshot all Slack, Teams, Google Chat, or Discord conversations that discuss your performance, complaints you filed, or conversations related to your termination before losing access.

Export Performance Review Documents: Screenshot or export your performance reviews, goal sheets, 360-feedback, and any written commendations from Workday, BambooHR, Lattice, or whatever performance management system your employer used.

Screenshot HR and Benefits Records: Capture records of any leave requests, accommodation requests, benefits information, and HR complaints you filed through internal systems before your company access is terminated.

Include Full Context in Every Screenshot: Ensure each screenshot captures the date, time, sender and recipient fields, and URL bar in the browser to establish clear authenticity and provenance of the evidence.

Use Your Phone Camera as a Backup: Photograph your screen with your phone instead of using a screenshot tool whenever possible, since phone photos are harder to claim were digitally altered or manipulated.

Screenshot Document Metadata Properties: Capture document properties showing author, creation date, and edit history by taking screenshots of file information panels, as this establishes an authentic timeline of when records were created or changed.

Document Any Evidence Deletion Attempts: Screenshot any system access warnings, disappearing messages, emails that show deleted status, or notifications about revoked access to build a record of potential destruction of evidence.

Avoid Unauthorized System Access: Do not attempt to access company systems, email accounts, or databases after your authorization has been revoked, as unauthorized access can undermine your legal standing and damage your credibility with attorneys.

Organize Everything in a Personal Case File: Create a secure, backed-up folder on your personal devices where you store all screenshots, exports, and documentation organized by date and category to present a clear narrative when meeting with an attorney.

Keep Records of Witness Information: Write down names, contact information, and brief notes about colleagues who witnessed the circumstances surrounding your termination or your prior complaints, as their testimony may support your case.

Preserve Physical Documentation: Collect and photograph any physical documents you received or signed during your employment, including your termination letter, performance improvement plans, and any written warnings or commendations.
